o.text: From Proto-Common Turkic *bulak. Cognate with Turkish bulak, Tatar bolaq, Uzbek buloq.
From Persian وطنپرست (vatan-parast); equivalent to vətən (“homeland”) + -pərəst.

From buraxıl + -ış.
Virtually all senses developed either as a calque or as a semantic loan from Russian вы́пуск (výpusk), за́пуск (zápusk), до́пуск (dópusk) or про́пуск (própusk).
From Russian кайф (kajf), from Arabic كَيْف (kayf, “pleasure”). Doublet of kef.

Izafet II compound of əmək + mühacir.
Likely a calque of Russian трудово́й мигра́нт (trudovój migránt).
